summary: Iteration 4 backend testing - 13/14 PASSED (1 SKIPPED, 0 FAILED). All P0 event-loop responsiveness fixes are working correctly. Concurrent /api/health and /api/auth/login calls during a 134-chunk document ingestion stayed well under the 2s SLA (health max=0.135s, login max=0.341s, 0 errors across 10 iterations). Async password hashing/verification works on login + register. /api/health no longer touches qdrant; new /api/health/qdrant returns qdrant=healthy. critical_code_review_comments: Good: /api/health stays purely local (no qdrant network/file call) so it's always sub-150ms even during heavy ingestion; qdrant status correctly split to /api/health/qdrant.
Good: hash_password_async / verify_password_async wrappers offload bcrypt from the event loop; login latency stayed ~330ms even with concurrent ingestion.
Good: vector_store.upsert_chunks BATCH=64 + asyncio.sleep(0) between batches handles 134-chunk doc cleanly; ingestion finished under ~60s with no errors.
Good: asyncio.to_thread wrapping for file reads in document_routes.py prevents large-file disk IO from blocking the loop.

rca_of_the_issue.original_p0: Synchronous CPU-bound operations (bcrypt hashing for auth, fastembed embedding generation, large file reads, single-shot qdrant upsert of all chunks) were blocking the asyncio event loop for the entire duration of doc ingestion, causing /api/health and /api/auth/login to hang.
rca_of_the_issue.fix_validated: Event loop now stays responsive: (1) bcrypt moved to thread pool via hash_password_async / verify_password_async; (2) file reads moved to asyncio.to_thread; (3) fastembed ONNX threadpool capped via embed_onnx_threads=half-cores leaving headroom for the event loop; (4) qdrant upsert batched (BATCH=64) with asyncio.sleep(0) yields between batches; (5) /api/health no longer touches qdrant (separate /api/health/qdrant route). Measured: <0.35s p95 for login and <0.15s p95 for health during ingestion of a 134-chunk doc - well within the 2s SLA.
